findings.title: Undefined or undocumented type alias 'HooksInputType'
findings.description: The diff introduces a new type `HooksInputType` and changes the annotation for `hooks` from `HooksType` to `HooksInputType | None` in both `_types.py` and `sessions.py`. However, the definition of `HooksInputType` is not visible in the provided diff. If `HooksInputType` is not already defined in the file, this will cause a `NameError` or `TypeError` at runtime or type-checking time. Furthermore, the meaning of `HooksInputType` vs `HooksType` is unclear from the diff alone, making it difficult for consumers to understand the API contract.
findings.suggestion: Ensure `HooksInputType` is properly defined in `src/requests/_types.py` before it is referenced. Add a docstring or comment explaining the difference between `HooksInputType` and `HooksType` (e.g., `HooksInputType` might be the user-facing input, while `HooksType` is the internal normalized structure). Update the public API documentation for `Session.request()` and `requests.request()` to reflect the new allowed types for the `hooks` parameter.

findings.title: Long parameter list in Session.request API
findings.description: The API contract for `hooks` is inconsistent. The `requests` library generally expects `hooks` to be a dictionary or `None`. While `HooksInputType` likely allows for a single callable or a list, mixing `None` into the type hint via union `| None` when the default is also `None` is a common pattern, but the broader issue is the lack of a unified `RequestOptions` or `ResponseOptions` dataclass. The `Session.request` method (implied by the context of `sessions.py` and `requests.py`) has a very long parameter list (over 10 parameters: `url`, `method`, `params`, `data`, `headers`, `cookies`, `files`, `auth`, `timeout`, `allow_redirects`, `proxies`, `hooks`, `stream`, `verify`, `cert`, `json`, `params`...). This violates the principle of low parameter count and makes the API fragile and difficult to use without keyword arguments. It also creates a high cognitive load for implementers of third-party libraries or testing mocks.
findings.suggestion: Consider introducing an `AdvancedOptions` or `RequestConfig` dataclass/NamedTuple to group less frequently used parameters (like `proxies`, `hooks`, `verify`, `cert`, `stream`). This would reduce the parameter count of `Session.request` and `requests.request` to a more manageable number (URL, Method, Data/Payload, Headers) while keeping the backward-compatible signature by allowing the new object as a final parameter or maintaining the current signature but encouraging internal refactoring. This improves API contract clarity and testability.

findings.title: No performance issues in type annotation changes
findings.description: This change is a type annotation update that moves `hooks` to `HooksInputType | None`. There are no performance, memory, algorithmic, concurrency, or caching implications in the diff itself.
findings.suggestion: No performance impact detected from this diff. It is purely a type-hint improvement. Ensure that `HooksInputType` and `HooksType` are properly defined and that no expensive computations are triggered during type checking at runtime (they are not, since `TYPE_CHECKING` blocks are excluded at runtime).
